question: Evaluate $\sin^{-1}\left(\sin\dfrac{7\pi}{6}\right)+\cos^{-1}\left(\cos\dfrac{5\pi}{3}\right)+\tan^{-1}\left(\tan\dfrac{3\pi}{4}\right)$ by reducing each angle to the appropriate principal-value branch and justify every reduction.
explanation:
Principal-Value Restrictions
The principal-value ranges are
$$\sin^{-1}x\in\left[-\frac{\pi}{2},\frac{\pi}{2}\right],\qquad\cos^{-1}x\in[0,\pi],\qquad\tan^{-1}x\in\left(-\frac{\pi}{2},\frac{\pi}{2}\right)$$

Evaluation
Since
$$\sin\frac{7\pi}{6}=-\frac{1}{2}$$
and $-\dfrac{\pi}{6}$ lies in the principal range of $\sin^{-1}$,
$$\sin^{-1}\left(\sin\frac{7\pi}{6}\right)=\sin^{-1}\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)=-\frac{\pi}{6}$$
Also,
$$\cos\frac{5\pi}{3}=\frac{1}{2}$$
Since $\dfrac{\pi}{3}\in[0,\pi]$,
$$\cos^{-1}\left(\cos\frac{5\pi}{3}\right)=\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)=\frac{\pi}{3}$$
Further,
$$\tan\frac{3\pi}{4}=-1$$
Since $-\dfrac{\pi}{4}$ lies in the principal range of $\tan^{-1}$,
$$\tan^{-1}\left(\tan\frac{3\pi}{4}\right)=\tan^{-1}(-1)=-\frac{\pi}{4}$$

Simplification
Therefore, the required expression equals
$$-\frac{\pi}{6}+\frac{\pi}{3}-\frac{\pi}{4}$$
$$=\frac{-2\pi+4\pi-3\pi}{12}=-\frac{\pi}{12}$$

Final Result
The value of the given expression is $-\dfrac{\pi}{12}$.

options.A: The principal values are $-\dfrac{\pi}{6}$, $\dfrac{\pi}{3}$ and $-\dfrac{\pi}{4}$, respectively; hence, the value is $-\dfrac{\pi}{12}$
options.B: The principal values are $\dfrac{\pi}{6}$, $\dfrac{\pi}{3}$ and $\dfrac{\pi}{4}$, respectively; hence, the value is $\dfrac{3\pi}{4}$
options.C: The principal values are $-\dfrac{\pi}{6}$, $\dfrac{5\pi}{3}$ and $-\dfrac{\pi}{4}$, respectively; hence, the value is $\dfrac{5\pi}{4}$
options.D: The principal values are $\dfrac{7\pi}{6}$, $\dfrac{\pi}{3}$ and $\dfrac{3\pi}{4}$, respectively; hence, the value is $\dfrac{9\pi}{4}$
